question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior for risky tool calls?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the fix defines a new config surface and core authorization boundary that automation cannot choose safely for all operators and channels.

options.title: Design the core gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Keep plugin-only approvals
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and require operators or plugins to enforce contextual approval through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies.

options.title: Fold into broader policy work
options.body: Wait for related action-level deny, response-gate, MCP consent, and HITL interrupt designs to converge before adding another config surface.

recommendation.title: Design the core gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests around existing plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and core agent execution semantics, matching the product/security routing evidence.
